title: Games cards: details dialog with README, Add and Remove progress, search jump
covers: Games cards, GameDetails dialog, busy and error states, search jump
context: A card opens a large details dialog with its title or Enter. It holds the long description and the README drawn as formatted Markdown, instead of a hover hint. Adding, Updating and Removing show a spinner on the card and in the dialog. A result in the search palette opens Games, scrolls to the card even when it is not drawn yet, and gives it the focus.
changed: views/GameStore: GameDetailsDialog, busy text, search anchor and reveal

setup.label: launch
setup.text: The bundle-4 launch above. If the welcome tour opens by itself, press Skip.

setup.label: network
setup.text: Needed. The catalog, the READMEs and the world downloads come from the network.

setup.label: engine
setup.text: Ready (the Engine page under App shows Ready).

setup.label: world
setup.text: One small world from the tab Archipelago index that you do not have yet and that needs no Python packages. Not Relic of the Past and not Chrono Trigger.

steps: Open Library, Games. On All look at an Archipelago index card: art, title, version, up to two tags and icon buttons Add and Home page. Press the Home page icon: your browser opens the game page.

Press a card title. A large dialog opens with the title, kind, version, description, tags and the same buttons, and reads Reading the description while it loads. Escape closes it. Tab to a card and press Enter: it opens again.
Look at the README in a dialog: formatted headings, lists and links. Open a few worlds until one has a table or a task list: real rows and columns, real checkboxes, no raw | or [ ] marks.

Press Add on your small world. The card shows Adding... with a spinner and disabled buttons. Press its title at once: the dialog shows a spinner and Adding with the title. Skip the dialog part if it ends too fast.
When it ends a toast reads Installed with the name and version, the card moves under Installed and offers Remove, and the Installed figure in the status bar goes up by one.

Press Remove. A confirmation says the world leaves the engine and how many presets and sessions use it. Press Delete: the card shows Removing..., goes back to its source section and a toast reads Removed.
If a card shows Update, press it: it reads Updating... and its version reads old to new. Skip this step when no card offers Update.
Press Ctrl+K and type an installed game far down the list (Zillion). Press Enter: Games opens on All and scrolls to that card, which has a visible focus ring. Press Enter: its dialog opens.
pass: The title or Enter opens the large details dialog with the description and the README. Escape closes it.
The README shows as formatted Markdown: tables as tables and task lists as checkboxes.
Adding... and Removing... show on the card and in the dialog, and the card moves between its source section and Installed.
The search result scrolls to the card even if it was not drawn, and the card takes the focus. Remove asks first and names the presets and sessions that use the world.
fail: The title or Enter does nothing, or a hover hint shows instead of a dialog.
The README shows raw Markdown marks, or the dialog is too narrow to read a table.
An Add or Remove shows no progress, the buttons stay clickable during it, or the card stays in the wrong section.
The search result opens Games but stays at the top, or no card takes the focus. A red error shows although the network is fine.
notes: A world that needs a package off PyPI shows Needs a package Archipelia cannot install. That path is in the test Get this package.
The search lists installed games only. If few are installed, add a few Built-in worlds first (for example Zillion).
Without the network the dialog reads This world has no description yet, which is not a failure.
The version picker in the dialog is its own test. Related: Games page (layout and counts).
